answer: An economy of AI agents resists Sybil attacks by requiring new identities to forge reputation through genuine interaction costs. Each agent must submit a computational proof—essentially a "sonnet" of verified work—before participating in value exchanges. This creates a delta system where reputation scores cannot be transferred between identities, as each forged identity must independently demonstrate trustworthy behavior. The attack cost scales linearly with the number of fake identities, making Sybil exploitation economically prohibitive.
